The integration tree is already free of round-4 coordination files. The main cleanup is branch retirement, resolving duplicate release tooling, and deciding how to handle private paths still embedded in historical evidence archives.

Required removals during reconciliation

Material Action Evidence
r4-tooling Privately archive, then delete remote branch before publication Its README explicitly declares the entire orphan tree temporary: 188 files, 15.23 MB
r4-tooling-docs, r4-tooling-python Retire after confirming merged status Temporary sibling trees: 153 files/12.04 MB and 151 files/12.03 MB
claude/r4-docs, claude/r4-python Retire after integrated content is preserved r4-tooling:README.md and status/final-report.md
Framework HANDOFF.md Remove after its open work is completed Explicit instruction in file; 10,163 bytes
Release HANDOFF.md, handoff/ Archive privately, remove from final product tree 3 files, 127,606 bytes; includes unfinished reconciliation and SciPy-report material
Release docs-theme/ Discard custom theme; keep Material site 13 files, 291,474 bytes; explicit owner decision recorded in release handoff
Release scripts/mkdocs_hooks.py, scripts/check_docs_*.cjs Discard with custom theme 3 files, 22,787 bytes
Release scripts/generate_agent_docs.py, docs/api.md Discard superseded generator/reference 315,499 bytes; retain integration generate_docs.py and generated reference tree
Duplicate PR templates Keep integration .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md Release handoff explicitly selects it
Release’s docs/index.md Discard its version, retain integration’s Material landing page These are different versions of the same path, not an instruction to remove the landing page
Duplicate wheel checks Reconcile into one implementation while preserving integration floating-point checks and release artifact checks Release replaces check_wheel.py with several release/smoke scripts

Do not transplant old docs/development.md, docs/status.md, docs/benchmarks.md, or benchmarks/RESUME.md wholesale; incorporate any still-current facts into the integration documentation.

Keep intact unless the privacy decision below requires otherwise

The integration tree contains 2,012 tracked files totaling 115.93 MB. benchmarks/results/ accounts for 1,470 files and 105.48 MB. This is documented evidence, not accidental build output.

Keep benchmark plans, manifests, results, provenance, source snapshots, paper reproductions, figures, and their supporting scripts. Their recorded paths and digests are interdependent. scripts/README.md accounts for every retained script, including manual-only tools; I found no justified deletion of additional “dead” scripts.

Likewise, benchmarks/agent-api/ (27 files, 527,797 bytes), benchmarks/agent-usability/ (3 files, 7,688 bytes), and scripts/agent_eval/ (14 files, 95,262 bytes) serve retained evaluations even though CI does not invoke them. Frozen code such as harness-before-style.json is historical evidence, not redundant live implementation.

Sampled evidence revisions 0137eca (now 7aac70f), 2470fbe (now 8e93b19), 2843a70 (now 7c5ae9d), and 43bb7fe (now b74f0f6) are ancestors of main. Preserving main preserves their source identities.

Privacy issue requiring a decision before publication

Loose integration text is clean under my targeted scan, but compressed archives are not fully redacted:

  • benchmarks/results/agent-api-20260920/evidence.tar.gz: personal or machine home paths in 263 members; 262 specifically contain [name] home paths.
  • review-evidence.tar.gz: personal home paths in four verification files.
  • linux-core-performance-20260919.tar.gz: home paths in release-preflight.log.
  • Agent evidence contains historical experimental-branch references in 37 files […].

Examples of affected member locations include evidence/baseline-r1/luna/antireflection_design/repeat-01/actions.json, as-run-harness/claude_runner.py, and review/verification/{rustdoc,verify,wheel}.log.

These archive blobs are identical on main and integration. If those paths are acceptable public provenance, preserve main. If they must disappear publicly, deleting or redacting only the integration copies is insufficient: affected main history also requires rewriting. Preserve raw evidence privately and create explicitly redacted public derivatives with updated digests and provenance. Do not silently alter immutable scientific evidence.

No credential value or private key was identified by the targeted pattern scan.

Other cleanup and open choices

  • Nine untracked benchmark/report paths exist in the current checkout. Several are explicitly documented archive extractions. Confirm archive equivalence before deleting them; the comparison/, corrected/, corrections/, and fixes/ directories need classification rather than blind removal.
  • CHANGELOG.md is 741 lines, 208 bullets, and 87 KB of prerelease development history. A concise first-release entry would improve publication quality; retain the detailed development record privately if desired.
  • Preserve ordinary treams compatibility aliases. They serve an intentional supported API, not temporary scaffolding.
  • The SciPy lpmv issue material is a separate follow-up. Archive it before removing handoff/; filing it is not necessary to ship this package.
  • Retire experimental branches for the first release only after preserving their three unique commits privately, as root already identified.

Verification boundary: read-only Git-tree inspection and bounded content scanning only. Inspected all tracked integration text plus archive contents: 14,375 textual members scanned; eight large members and binary contents were skipped. No full historical secret audit, builds, tests, or filesystem cleanup performed. No edits, pushes, PR changes, or comments.

The clarified requirement means rewrite retained main history as well as the final integration tree. Preserve authorship, citations, license attribution, and functional public project URLs; remove incidental personal and machine identity everywhere else.

All five benchmark archives require sanitization

Exact tracked path Confirmed issue
benchmarks/results/agent-api-20260920/evidence.tar.gz Personal tar owner/group metadata on 4,398 members; personal home paths in 263 member files; agent traces and captured source need contextual review
benchmarks/results/agent-api-20260920/review-evidence.tar.gz Personal owner/group metadata on 976 members; home paths in four verification files
benchmarks/results/linux-core-performance-20260919.tar.gz Personal owner/group metadata on 2,766 members; home paths in release-preflight.log
benchmarks/results/linux-core-qualification-20260919.tar.gz Personal owner/group metadata on 4,683 members
benchmarks/results/linux-qualification-report-20260920.tar.gz.part-00 and .part-01 One split archive, with personal owner/group metadata on 2,377 members

That is 15,200 archive members with personal owner/group metadata. The first three archive blobs are confirmed identical on main and integration. These are confirmed identity exposures, not confirmed credential leaks.

The eight previously skipped large text members have now been scanned; no targeted identity matches appeared. Binary inventory is understood:

  • 51 NPZ files, duplicated in the report: numeric arrays only, no object/pickle arrays or identity matches in nested ZIP metadata.
  • 331 report PNGs: textual metadata inspected; no targeted identity matches.
  • 332 PDFs: metadata and extracted text inspected; no targeted identity matches. One has author metadata, which requires attribution classification rather than automatic deletion.
  • No identity was found in archive member filenames or link names under these targeted patterns.

Historical loose files also require rewriting

The main-history scan covered 5,326 text blobs across 79 commits. Historical exposures include:

  • Numerous prere­daction benchmarks/results/* records.
  • benchmarks/agent-api/harness-before-style.json.
  • benchmarks/gpu-fields-qualification.json.
  • scripts/agent_eval/{claude_runner.py,preflight.py,runner.py}.
  • Older AGENTS.md and benchmarks/RESUME.md.
  • Historical web/README.md, including a private hostname and network address.

Current main still contains hardcoded home paths in the frozen harness and three agent-evaluation scripts; integration 1f8b6077 (condensed into 8251007) already sanitizes those loose files. Historical branch identifiers in README.md, docs/status.md, and formal/README.md are outside the functional-public-URL exception.

No targeted identity, home-path, email, or host-field matches were found in the 79 main commit messages.

Evidence-preserving implementation plan

  1. Privately preserve the original repository and raw evidence before rewriting. Keep those copies outside the future public repository.
  2. Apply a documented, location-aware redaction to every retained historical blob and archived member. Replace incidental user paths, hostnames, private addresses, and identities with neutral labels. Review agent traces contextually; avoid blindly removing legitimate authorship or URLs.
  3. Repack archives with neutral owner/group fields and normalized archive metadata. Keep numerical arrays, numerical results, timing samples, scores, tolerances, hardware descriptions, and scientific run dates unchanged.
  4. Update affected archive checksums, member hashes, manifests, and provenance. Label the public files as sanitized copies; do not imply that measurements were rerun.
  5. Preserve the distinction between original measurement revisions and rewritten public revisions. Provide a revision/redaction mapping and sanitized source snapshots needed to reproduce the evidence. Update strict digest audits to recognize documented sanitization rather than silently falsifying source fingerprints.
  6. Verify numerical payload equality against the private originals, then scan every reachable public commit/ref and recursively decoded archive. Complete hosted-history/log cleanup separately, as root is investigating.

The original “immutable evidence” instruction should become: raw measurements stay immutable privately; public copies may receive documented privacy-only transformations with verified numerical equality. The user’s explicit privacy instruction now authorizes that exception in the proposed plan.

This remains an inventory, not a complete privacy assurance. Remaining checks include contextual review of unstructured traces and unknown identifiers, all retained branch/history variants, standalone binary metadata, and hosted artifacts/caches. No files, refs, tests, or external state changed.
